sentences.text:
This misc. appeal u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 198 has been filed by appellants-claimants seeking enhancement of compensation amount by taking exception to the Award dated 08/09/2016 passed by Member, MACT, District- Gwalior (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.
231/2014, whereby the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 4,35,000 along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization in favour of claimants on account of death of Bharat Singh (son of appellants) in a motor accident.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3 . Counsel for appellants submitted that compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal by a s s e s s i n g t h e i n c o m e o f d e c e a s e d t o t h e t u n e o f N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025

: MPHC-GWL:24747 2 MA-1325-2016 Rs.4000/- per month is inadequate and is on lower side,
as deceased-Bharat Singh was working as a Cleaner of truck at the time of accident, therefore, his income must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.

It is further submitted that Claims Tribunal has adopted the multiplier of "15" in its Award, whereas, looking to age of deceased-Bharat Singh,
Claims Tribunal ought to have have adopted the multiplier of "16".
Counsel for appellants further submitted that Claims Tribunal has erred in not awarding any future prospect at the time of awarding compensation in favour of claimants.

Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants Smt. Rama vs Raghvendra Singh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57339194/
1 contended that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding reasonable amount in other heads i.e. loss of estate, loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

5. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
6.
After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased is on lower side.

In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.5,845/- per month of an unskilled labour instead of Rs.4,000/- per month which has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24747 3 MA-1325-2016 wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

7. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 40% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121

8.

Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Rs 5,845/- per month X12=70  Income  annum  Future Prospects@40% Rs. 28,056/-

Total income Rs.98,196/-
 Dependency 1/2 Rs.49,098/-
 Loss of Income Rs.49,098 X 18= 8,83,764/-
Other Heads:-

Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 2 = Rs. 80,000/
 Loss of Estate and funeral  Rs.30,000/-
 expenses  Total Compensation = Rs 9.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case i s Rs.9,93,764/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.4,35,000/-.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are Smt. Rama vs Raghvendra Singh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57339194/
2 entitled to an NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24747 4 MA-1325-2016 additional sum of Rs. 5,58,764/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs. 5,58,764/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
